executiveSummary: Apeldoorn's generated identity and 2025 administrative data are coherent: GM0200 is placed in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland, its centre lies within the generalized boundary, and 95 CBS neighbourhoods, 12 BAG woonplaatsen, 25 BRT settlements, 13 signed-road logical links, three ProRail stations and 243 GTFS stop areas are retained. The neighbourhood population sum differs from the official 168,551 total by only 16 people (-0.009%), and the allocator reconciles every service back to the official total without inventing residents in zero-resident business and nature areas. The complete deterministic contract passes for ten hazards, six checkpoints and eight services, including exact zero-intensity behavior, bounded state, causal-ledger closure, selected-layer invariance and sustained-water recovery guards. The audit is nevertheless correction-required. The named Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset gives nearly all of Apeldoorn a sustained direct flood screen of 2.131206 internal units, 94,578 affected people-equivalent and critical service pressure at T+72, while the municipality's official environment assessment says flood danger is small and only the eastern side has a very small probability from the IJssel. This is a proximity-derived screen, not a named LIWO hydraulic scenario. Seven materially different hazards also reuse the exact same neighbourhood rank, led by Kuipersveld and Agrarisch gebied Wiesel, because one scenario-independent seeded multiplier substitutes for local exposure. That conflicts with documented western urban cloudburst hotspots and the large, forested Veluwe wildfire exposure, including VNOG's operational Loenen/A50/N786 scenario. Public HWH/PDOK register context now exposes 520 in-boundary water assets but deliberately does not turn those points into live capacity or causal topology. Physical electricity, drinking-water, wastewater, gas, telecom, facility, fuel, staffing and restoration topology remains unavailable or security-sensitive and is not fabricated; exact service values are transparent planning outputs, not forecasts or operator commitments.

supports: Official GM0200 population 168,551, density 496 per square kilometre, 37,982 residents aged 65+ and 29,081 one-person households.
Municipality, district and neighbourhood attributes and their rounding, null and disclosure semantics.
Machine-readable OData; CBS open data are reusable under CC BY 4.0 and this table is an annual edition.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025 and Gebiedsindelingen OGC APIs
supports: Official generalized municipality, district and neighbourhood geometry used for centre containment and 95-neighbourhood membership.
The generated regional bundle separately cites BAG woonplaatsen, CBS safety-region boundaries, BRT settlements, RWS NWB, ProRail and OVapi GTFS provenance.
CBS geometry is CC BY 4.0 and annual; BAG/PDOK source records are Public Domain Mark 1.0 where stated in the generated provenance.

evidenceSources.title: Omgevingsvisie Apeldoorn – Aanvulling Omgevingseffectrapport, bijlage 2 van 2
supports: Extreme-cloudburst water nuisance is concentrated in lower western parts of the city, including Staatsliedenkwartier, Apeldoorn Zuidwest, Sprengenbos, Kerschoten and Ugchelen, with additional issues in villages and on the Veluwe.
Heat and drought are broad municipal concerns.
Flood safety is assessed as good: danger from the IJssel is not large and only the eastern side has a very small flood probability.
The PDF is authoritative local planning evidence but not a machine-ready event raster; its page carries no model-suitable update cadence or explicit data licence.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, bijlagenboek
supports: Named LIWO flood scenarios concern dike rings and breach locations rather than a municipality-wide Apeldoorn depth field.
Apeldoorn contains 19,480 hectares of nature-fire area, the largest municipal value in the VNOG table.

The Loenen scenario identifies A50 exit 23, N786, heath and conifer fuel, difficult access, dry water points, 150 kV and telecom dependencies, Vitens Schalterberg, accommodation/care sites and about 1,500 evacuees in the first operational period.

The drinking-water contamination scenario covers 9,500 connections and 31,633 people, mainly between Paleis Het Loo, Kerschoten, Indische buurt and Berg en Bos, with source discovery on day four and normalization on day six.
This periodically adopted official profile is a document, not a public real-time incident or infrastructure API; no reusable machine-data licence is stated.

evidenceSources.title: Landelijk Informatiesysteem Water en Overstromingen (LIWO)
supports: Professional scenario layers for flooding, intended for expert interpretation rather than generic distance-to-river conversion.
Machine endpoints are available at https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/api/v2 and https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows.

Updates are release-based rather than on a fixed cadence; the inspected public landing/configuration does not state a general redistribution licence, so every selected layer requires terms review and pinned version metadata.

evidenceSources.title: ISOR brandbaar natuurgebied
supports: Public machine-readable polygons for burnable natural areas of at least 100 hectares through WFS layer ISOR_RK:isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied at https://servicespub.risicokaart.nl/geoserver/ISOR_RK/wfs.
A focused query returned eight GM0200-supplied records, but old validity dates and a test-like feature show why freshness, object status and provenance must be validated before simulation use.
CC BY 4.0; record updates are contributor-driven and the catalogue does not promise a fixed publication cadence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water authorities / PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Waterschappen Kunstwerken IMWA and Waterketen DAMO OGC APIs
supports: Public surface-water pumps, weirs and sluices, supplemented by the Waterketen DAMO API at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 for sewer pumps and wastewater-treatment plants.
The current national display-only snapshot contains 520 points within GM0200: 503 weirs, eight surface-water pumping stations, six sewer pumping stations, two sluices and RWZI Apeldoorn.
CC BY-SA 4.0; Kunstwerken IMWA is published weekly, while Waterketen DAMO's provider cadence is stated as unknown and contributor completeness varies.
Register presence and name do not establish live status, capacity, control, catchment, backup or causal service availability.

evidenceSources.title: 10-minute in-situ meteorological observations, version 1.0
supports: Machine-readable observed wind, temperature, precipitation and related variables through the KNMI Data Platform and EDR API at https://api.dataplatform.knmi.nl/edr/v1/docs.
CC BY 4.0, reported every ten minutes on a continual cadence; delayed or missing updates can extend to seven days and observations are not forecasts.
A suitable event-forcing input for storm, rain, heat and winter context, but insufficient by itself for local flood hydraulics, wildfire spread or service failure.

identity.summary: GM0200, Apeldoorn, Gelderland and safety region Noord- en Oost-Gelderland agree across the manifest, generated bundles and official 2025 sources.
notes: Generated feature id, bundle code, bundle name, province and safety-region membership all match.
The generated centre [5.902579956313215, 52.185728626354624] lies inside the generalized 2025 municipality boundary.
Exactly one municipality and one safety-region record resolve for the code.

geography.summary: The municipality centre, all 95 neighbourhood records and all 12 BAG woonplaats centres pass the generated containment and membership checks.
notes: No BAG woonplaats centre lies outside the generalized municipality boundary and the context helper reports no review flags.

The administrative polygons do not encode terrain, IJssel connectivity, stream/catchment flow, forest fuel, heat, wind exposure or emergency access; those are calibration limitations rather than boundary errors.

demography.summary: The generated municipality record reproduces the official 2025 population and small-area counts reconcile within expected CBS rounding.
notes: Official/generated population is 168,551, density 496/km², age 65+ 37,982 or 22.5%, and one-person households 29,081.
Published neighbourhood population sums to 168,535, 16 below the municipality total or -0.009%; neighbourhood households sum to 76,910 and age 65+ to 37,970.
The allocator scales published neighbourhood weights to the exact municipality population without rewriting the source observations.

regionalDetail.summary: All 95 neighbourhoods and 36 declared fields are structurally retained, but legitimate CBS null coverage remains substantial for some indicators.
notes: Core demographics, households, homes, non-residential buildings, businesses, cars and land/water area cover 95/95 neighbourhoods.
Average home value and housing tenure/type cover 86/95; household size 93/95; cars per household 75/95; social indicators 87/95; doctor and supermarket distance 90/95.
District-heating percentage and public charging points cover 0/95 and correctly remain unavailable rather than being coerced to zero.
The largest published neighbourhoods are Zuidbroek - Mozaïek & Rooster (6,625), Orden (6,380), Binnenstad (6,005), Woudhuis (5,865) and Matenveld (5,610).

settlements.summary: Twelve BAG woonplaatsen and 25 BRT settlement features provide coherent but non-equivalent place context.
notes: The BAG names are Apeldoorn, Beekbergen, Beemte Broekland, Hoenderloo, Hoog Soeren, Klarenbeek, Lieren, Loenen, Radio Kootwijk, Uddel, Ugchelen and Wenum Wiesel.
BRT settlement types comprise five buurtschappen, two deelkernen, six gehuchten and twelve woonkernen.
Settlement labels are not treated as current occupancy, an evacuation count or a demographic reconciliation target.

transport.summary: Thirteen signed NWB logical links, three ProRail stations and 243 GTFS stop areas are coherent, but only road-derived logical transfers enter the service solver.
notes: The links reach eight unique neighbours through A1, A50, N304, N345, N310, N786, N789, N804 and N344 records; nominal 260/150 capacities are synthetic transfer units, not vehicles per hour.
Apeldoorn, Apeldoorn De Maten and Apeldoorn Osseveld station points and 243 transit stop areas are display context, not rail, passenger, evacuation or supply graph capacity.
VNOG's Loenen wildfire case specifically depends on access via A50 exit 23 and N786, a mode and location specificity absent from the generic municipal route state.

emergencyContext.summary: Official sources establish specific flood, cloudburst, wildfire, drinking-water and transport mechanisms, but live response resources and physical operator topology are not publicly available to the model.
notes: The model does not represent VNOG's Loenen fuel/access/water/evacuation conditions or the named multi-day drinking-water contamination case.
The new public water-asset context is appropriately register-only and affectsSimulation=false; it does not claim operational state.

No complete public source supplies current crews, fire appliances, feeder switching, water pressure zones, sewer controls, gas pressure districts, telecom backhaul, facility beds/staff, emergency stocks, backup autonomy or restoration priority.

scenarioMatrix.summary: The repaired current build completes all ten canonical presets at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services without missing or non-finite output.
notes: Reproduction: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0200 pnpm audit:model; one file and two tests passed in 27.22 seconds on 2 September 2026, with test execution 27.05 seconds. The national harness is recorded green for 342 municipalities × 10 scenarios × 6 checkpoints × 8 services.

Peak/current scenario review covers severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound. Peak severity is respectively 0.548646, 0.400214, 0.668227, 0, 0.476962, 0.756920, 0.536584, 0.045531, 0.273887 and 0.867899.

Canonical forcing durations are 18, 12, 168, 42, 336, 36, 48, 10, 40 and 54 hours in the same order. Coastal direct hazard remains zero for inland Apeldoorn, although preset wind still creates a modest attributable service burden.

At river T+72, the frame reports severity 0.668227, internal flood amplitude 2.131206, 94,578 affected people-equivalent, 5,676,787.6 event-attributable deprived person-hours and critical status, with mobility limiting at 0.366389 availability.

At compound T+24, severity is 0.865663, internal flood amplitude 0.350958, 108,541 affected people-equivalent and 1,548,830.1 event-attributable deprived person-hours; power is limiting at 0.280413 availability. These are deterministic pressure outputs, not observations.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, allocation/reconciliation, ledger monotonicity and selected-layer invariance pass.
notes: All service availability remains in [0,1]; event dimensions, demand, delivery, affected population and event-attributable deprived person-hours are non-negative; cumulative ledgers do not decrease.

At compound T+24 each of power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply has 95 local rows summing to 168,551 residents and 108,541 affected people-equivalent. Maximum absolute demand/delivery reconciliation error is about 6.4×10^-14.

For every preset/checkpoint, zero intensity returns exactly zero event dimensions, event severity, affected population and event-attributable deprived person-hours; seasonal ambient temperature remains separate context.
Zero-resident Bedrijvenpark Ecofactorij, Orderbos and Bosgebied Wiesel receive no invented residents but can retain small non-residential activity demand.

spatialPlausibility.summary: The finite municipal screens work, but seven unrelated active hazards reuse one exact seeded neighbourhood rank and the direct river screen is incompatible with the strongest local official evidence.
notes: At representative active checkpoints, severe storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Kuipersveld first, Agrarisch gebied Wiesel second, De Mheen third, Loenen fourth and Kerschoten-West fifth.
Code inspection traces this to a shared canonical seed and local hazard multiplier 0.82 + seededUnit(region id) × 0.36; the hazard type and source-specific exposure do not alter the order.

The official municipality assessment instead names western cloudburst hotspots, while VNOG identifies a Loenen/Veluwe fire mechanism and the municipality says direct IJssel flood probability is only very small on the east side.

Changing editable wildfire ignition changes municipal intensity but not the source-free local ranking; no fuel, wind direction, access, suppression water or visitor occupancy enters neighbourhood allocation.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight cascades execute with distinct coefficients, but their transfer and recovery state is aggregate and cannot be interpreted as operator topology or capacity.
notes: River T+72 availability is power 0.479734, water 0.456510, drainage 0.438906, gas 0.744594, telecom 0.504412, mobility 0.366389, facilities 0.376476 and supply 0.396421.
Compound T+24 availability is power 0.280413, water 0.338930, drainage 0.350776, gas 0.582937, telecom 0.342487, mobility 0.419657, facilities 0.619272 and supply 0.357760.
The same 13 NWB municipality-pair links are reused with transferSemantics=logical-proxy. Official water-register points, three rail stations and 243 stops do not become causal service edges.

VNOG documents cross-service consequences in the Loenen fire and drinking-water cases, but public evidence does not support exact feeder, pipe, pump-control, telecom, facility or restoration parameters.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, direct-service, dependency, intervention, network, allocation and reconciliation causes remain deterministic, closed and inspectable with proxy disclosures.
notes: The harness verifies changed-driver explanations, hazard/service/system ledger closure, matched zero-intensity accounting and identical repeated frames.
All official neighbourhoods intentionally have neutral priority 2 and isHub=false; no unsupported critical facility or physical utility relation is asserted.

A clean headless browser path selected Apeldoorn, river flood, T+72 and each of Overview, Hazard, Power, Water, Drainage, Gas, Telecom, Mobility, Facilities, People and Supply without console or page errors. The default-to-river-T+72-layer path required four operator activations.

The UI identified critical status, 37% minimum availability, mobility as limiting, 5.68 million attributable deprived person-hours and forcing continuing beyond 72 hours. It labels service capacity and failures as scenario assumptions; this disclosure does not validate the river footprint.

recovery72h.summary: Recovery mechanics respect active forcing and standing-water access guards through T+72, while locally calibrated repair and recession times remain unavailable.
notes: The river scenario remains forced and critical through T+72 and correctly does not perform generic repair while its internal water screen persists.
Compound retains internal flood amplitude 0.350958 and cyber disruption 0.0612 at T+72, remains critical and has 118,281 affected people-equivalent and 5,839,207 attributable deprived person-hours.

Storm, pluvial, winter and wildfire frames transition to recovering by T+48 and operational by T+72 without decreasing cumulative deprived person-hours; heat remains weakly forced at T+72 under its 336-hour duration.
These rules are conservative deterministic guards, not IJssel recession, forest-fire control, Vitens continuity, crew mobilization or facility restoration forecasts.

findings.summary: Generated identity and official municipality totals are coherent.
findings.evidence: The code, name, province, safety region, 2025 boundary/statistics editions and centre containment all agree. CBS gives 168,551 residents, while published neighbourhood rows sum to 168,535, a normal -0.009% small-area rounding difference that the allocator reconciles without rewriting source data.
findings.action: Retain source edition, retrieval time, null semantics and the explicit published-versus-allocated reconciliation in future refreshes.

findings.summary: Neighbourhood, place, settlement and zero-resident activity handling pass structural review.
findings.evidence: All 95 CBS neighbourhoods, 12 BAG woonplaatsen and 25 BRT settlements are retained. Core statistics have complete coverage, incomplete indicators stay null, and zero-resident areas do not gain residents while legitimate businesses and non-residential buildings may generate demand.
findings.action: Preserve the distinction among municipality, neighbourhood, BAG woonplaats and BRT settlement ontologies and retain activity-aware zero-resident tests.

findings.summary: The canonical major-river preset assigns unsupported sustained direct inundation stress across Apeldoorn.
findings.evidence: The T+12 through T+72 result holds an internal flood amplitude of 2.131206 and at T+72 reports 94,578 affected people-equivalent, critical status and mobility availability 0.366389. E03 says municipal flood danger is small, IJssel danger is not large and only the eastern side has a very small probability. E04's official scenarios are named dike-ring/breach cases and E05 provides hydraulic scenario layers. The model instead derives a finite proximity screen and labels its spatial evidence derived-screening; it is not a selected LIWO footprint or physical metre depth.
findings.action: Suppress direct GM0200 river depth/affected-area claims or mark them unsupported until an expert-selected, versioned LIWO/VNOG IJssel scenario intersects the municipality. Preserve separately evidenced indirect network effects and do not interpret suppression as an all-clear.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated hazards reuse one identical synthetic neighbourhood ranking.
findings.evidence: Severe storm, pluvial flood, river flood, heatwave, winter storm, cyberattack and wildfire all rank Kuipersveld, Agrarisch gebied Wiesel, De Mheen, Loenen and Kerschoten-West in the same first-through-fifth order. The code applies a common scenario seed and region-id multiplier; no hazard-specific local exposure changes the order. Official evidence distinguishes western city cloudburst depressions, broad heat/drought, an eastern IJssel edge and forested Loenen/Veluwe wildfire mechanisms.
findings.action: Replace the common rank with versioned hazard-specific local exposure adapters. Until source layers exist, label every neighbourhood pattern synthetic and prohibit hotspot language or apparent numeric precision.

findings.summary: Wildfire behavior omits the documented Loenen/Veluwe fuel, access, water and occupancy mechanism.
findings.evidence: E04 records 19,480 hectares of Apeldoorn nature-fire area and describes a Loenen incident near A50 exit 23/N786 involving heath/conifer fuel, 5–7 m/s north-easterly wind, dry water points, difficult access, utilities, accommodation/care sites and about 1,500 evacuees. The canonical T+24 frame reports severity 0.273887, fire intensity 0.2, smoke 0.3973 and 14,424 affected people-equivalent but places Loenen only fourth through the generic rank, with no fuel, wind-direction, road-access, suppression-water, visitor or facility state.
findings.action: Build a versioned Loenen/Veluwe operational fixture from public land cover, burnable-area and weather data plus the official VNOG narrative; represent visitor and facility occupancy as scenario inputs, not resident population.

findings.summary: Generic density and seeded variation miss the municipality's named western cloudburst hotspots and flow system.
findings.evidence: E03 names Staatsliedenkwartier, Apeldoorn Zuidwest, Sprengenbos, Kerschoten and Ugchelen as low-lying extreme-rain hotspots. The pluvial scenario instead uses the same local order as heat, cyber and wildfire and has no elevation, surface flow, sewer catchment, pump or storage relation. Kerschoten-West appears fifth, but that coincidence is produced by a shared seed rather than the official mechanism.
findings.action: Ingest an approved machine-readable municipal/waterboard stress-test grid with AHN/IMWA flow and catchment context; until its licence, vintage and units are confirmed, show normalized municipal stress rather than neighbourhood depth or hotspot accuracy.

findings.summary: One aggregate water availability state cannot represent VNOG's named Apeldoorn contamination and emergency-water sequence.
findings.evidence: E04 describes 9,500 connections and 31,633 people mainly between Paleis Het Loo, Kerschoten, Indische buurt and Berg en Bos, loss/boil advice and bottled-water pressure, effects on facilities, source discovery at the Amersfoortseweg reservoir on day four and normal service on day six. The first-72-hour model has no contamination/quality flag, advisory, affected pressure-zone aggregate, emergency-water demand or day-four investigation state.
findings.action: Add a versioned curated scenario fixture using only the public aggregate areas, counts and timeline, with separate quantity, quality, advisory and emergency-supply states. Keep Vitens pipes, valves, controls, exact reservoir security details and restoration commitments unknown unless explicitly authorized.

findings.summary: Public water-authority assets are now visible as non-causal register context with appropriate caveats.
findings.evidence: The compressed national HWH/PDOK snapshot contains 520 in-boundary register points: 503 weirs, eight surface-water pumps, six sewer pumps, two sluices and RWZI Apeldoorn. Source, publisher, retrieval and CC BY-SA metadata are retained and affectsSimulation=false prevents point presence or often-null capacity fields from becoming live availability.
findings.action: Keep the layer lazy, clustered and explicitly display-only; validate weekly Kunstwerken refreshes and variable Waterketen completeness, and never infer operating condition, flow direction, catchment or backup from a point.

findings.summary: Road-derived logical transfer is transparent but cannot substitute for multimodal or utility-specific continuity.
findings.evidence: All eight services reuse 13 NWB municipality-pair links. Three rail stations and 243 GTFS stop areas remain context only, and VNOG's A50/N786 access dependency cannot be tested as a local closure. Electricity, drinking water, drainage, gas and telecom cross-boundary zones do not follow road adjacency. The current logical-proxy label correctly avoids claiming otherwise.
findings.action: Add licensed event-valid mobility overlays and separately sourced aggregate utility zones only where publication permits. Retain synthetic logical transfer for unavailable or security-sensitive topology with explicit unknown capacity and no operator attribution.

findings.summary: Weather-related values are deterministic scenario forcing, not current observations or forecasts.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, coastal-wind, heat, winter, wildfire and compound values are bounded and reproducible, but no event-valid KNMI observation/forecast or local gridded forcing is selected. Earthquake is a small synthetic screen and cyber is a hypothetical disruption. The UI's scenario-assumption disclosure is correct.
findings.action: Allow optional pinned KNMI observation or forecast fixtures with location, issue/valid time, unit, uncertainty and missing-data behavior; retain deterministic synthetic forcing for exercises and never label it as a forecast.

findings.summary: Physical service topology, live assets and restoration resources are not publicly available at the fidelity implied by exact availability values.
findings.evidence: No consumed authoritative dataset provides Liander feeder/switch state, Vitens pressure-zone/pipe state, wastewater control topology, gas districts, telecom backhaul, facility beds/staff/backup, fuel, stocks, crews or repair priority. Public register and capacity-planning data can add context but not live resilience. The model uses disclosed aggregate coefficients and logical transfers instead of fabricating these details.
findings.action: Preserve unknown fields and uncertainty ranges, accept operator-authorized aggregates when available, and require provenance for every topology, backup and restoration claim. Do not reverse-engineer security-sensitive networks from public points.

findings.summary: The complete numerical, causal, recovery and UI interaction contract passes after the shared transient fault was repaired.
findings.evidence: The mandatory GM0200 gate passed one file/two tests in 27.22 seconds. Every scenario/checkpoint/service is finite and deterministic, local allocations reconcile, zero intensity is exact, causal ledgers close, cumulative harm is monotone and selected layers do not change the model. Headless interaction reached municipality, scenario, checkpoint and each of eleven views without console/page errors.
findings.action: Keep GM0200 and the national 342-municipality gate in regression runs, and preserve visible separation between official context, derived screening, synthetic assumptions and unsupported claims.

corrections.summary: Replace Apeldoorn's unsupported municipality-wide major-river screen with named hydraulic scenario geometry and an interim conservative exclusion.
corrections.validation: Immediately mark GM0200 direct river output unsupported or zero at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 unless a selected source footprint intersects; indirect network effects may remain and the UI must state that absence of a direct screen is not an all-clear. Preferred machine source: Rijkswaterstaat/WMCN LIWO catalogue/API https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/api/v2 and GeoServer OWS https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows, constrained to an expert-approved IJssel/dike-ring scenario referenced by E03/E04. LIWO updates by versioned releases rather than a fixed cadence (inspected application 2025.1.6); no general public redistribution licence is stated, so review each layer's terms and persist scenario id, layer id, version, retrieval time, resolution, units and expert approval. Never convert a distance screen to metres. Re-run unit, GM0200 and national ALL gates and assert no direct flood outside connected approved cells.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared seeded neighbourhood ordering with mechanism-specific Apeldoorn exposure, beginning with the documented Loenen/Veluwe wildfire case.
corrections.validation: Preferred machine sources: PDOK BRT TOP10NL terrain_vlak OGC API https://api.pdok.nl/brt/top10nl/ogc/v1 (CC BY 4.0, annual edition) for land-cover/fuel eligibility; Risicokaart WFS https://servicespub.risicokaart.nl/geoserver/ISOR_RK/wfs layer ISOR_RK:isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied (CC BY 4.0, contributor-driven with catalogue metadata updated 2024-10-16) for registered burnable areas; and KNMI EDR https://api.dataplatform.knmi.nl/edr/v1/docs (CC BY 4.0, observations every ten minutes, possible delays up to seven days) for event-valid weather. Validate feature status and exclude test/stale records before use. Encode VNOG Loenen/A50/N786 operational facts as a versioned curated fixture because no machine incident layer is published; preserve its documentary provenance and do not invent fuel load, occupancy, suppression capacity or utility topology. Assert hazard-specific neighbourhood ranks differ when source footprints differ and exact zero-intensity remains unchanged.

corrections.summary: Add source-governed pluvial and drainage context for the official western Apeldoorn cloudburst hotspots without turning asset registers into live hydraulics.
corrections.validation: Request a machine-readable municipal/Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe stress-test raster or vector for the E03 hotspots; no confirmed public API/licence/cadence was located, so do not digitize the PDF or manufacture depth. Integrate only an approved layer with licence, vintage, rainfall design event, elevation basis, units and coverage. Public supporting sources are PDOK HWH Kunstwerken IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 (CC BY-SA 4.0, weekly), Waterbeheergebieden IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterbeheergebieden-imwa/ogc/v1 (CC BY-SA 4.0, weekly) and Waterketen DAMO https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 (CC BY-SA 4.0, provider cadence unknown and contributor completeness variable). The 520 current points must remain display-only until catchment, direction, capacity, state and power/control dependencies are separately evidenced. Validate named hotspot intersections, null semantics and local/municipal reconciliation.

corrections.summary: Represent VNOG's public aggregate drinking-water contamination sequence as a quality-and-supply scenario while keeping sensitive Vitens topology unavailable.
corrections.validation: No licensed machine-readable public API was found for this scenario or for Vitens pressure zones/valves; use a manually reviewed, versioned fixture derived only from E04's public aggregates: 9,500 connections, 31,633 people, named broad areas, advisory/supply consequences, day-four source discovery and day-six normalization. Record VNOG edition 2025–2028, page references, review date and that reuse terms are not machine-published. Separate quality, quantity, boil advisory, emergency-water demand and facility effects; do not publish or infer pipe, valve, control, reservoir-security, backup or restoration topology. Tests must prevent double-counting affected residents and distinguish an exercise fixture from a current incident.

corrections.summary: Add event-valid public mobility and planning-capacity context while retaining explicit synthetic fallback for unavailable utility operations.
corrections.validation: For mobility, use NDW DATEX II live/planned situation feeds from https://opendata.ndw.nu/ and documentation at https://docs.ndw.nu/handleidingen/NCIS/WebportaalD2v3/ (NDW open-data/site content CC0 unless a product states otherwise; records update on change and pull guidance recommends 60-second polling), retaining record id, validity, direction, mode and retrieval time. For electricity planning context only, use Netbeheer Nederland's public capacity-map model https://modellen.netbeheernederland.nl/capaciteitskaart/2.1/index.html (open data; capacity and works quarterly, waiting-list fields monthly). Neither source supports live service availability, feeder topology or restoration. Preserve current CC0 NWB geometry/monthly snapshot for static routes, keep operator utility topology, controls, crews, backup, stock and repair time unknown unless authorized, and assert road closure does not automatically sever water, power, gas or telecom without a declared dependency.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic exercise-model audit of the first 72 hours, not a forecast, emergency instruction, legal flood assessment or operator service commitment.
The 2025 CBS and generalized PDOK boundary editions are administrative snapshots and can differ slightly from operational or cadastral boundaries.
CBS small-area counts are rounded/suppressed; null district-heating and charging fields are unknown, not zero.
BAG woonplaatsen and BRT settlements are contextual geometries and do not provide current occupancy or visitor counts.
LIWO scenario choice, hydraulic interpretation, breach probability and redistribution terms require domain-owner review; no unsourced metre-depth accuracy is claimed.
The municipality's PDF names cloudburst locations but is not a machine-readable depth grid; exact street or building impact remains unverified.
Nature-fire registrations can be stale or contributor/test records; fuel, moisture, suppression and plume behavior require event-valid validation.
KNMI ten-minute observations can be delayed/missing and are observations rather than forecasts or wildfire-spread products.
